family.tagline: A small rental, a drawing table, and a Core on the shelf.
family.story: Marisol illustrates and translates children's books from a rented cottage in Piedra Lisa. Her son Mateo, who is five, names every dragon she draws. Their drafts, drawings and bedtime stories sit on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Nico
companion.job: Opens LibreTranslate in its own browser and runs a first pass on a paragraph.
companion.limits: First pass only. Marisol edits every line.

popup.title: A parcel for a rented cottage
popup.body: A parcel waits at the cottage door. Marisol carries it straight to the shelf in the living room. The cottage is rented, so nothing here needs a screwdriver.

popup.title: Mateo opens the parcel
popup.body: Mateo opens the parcel. Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: One plug, one button
popup.body: Marisol plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Marisol joins the Core's own network on her phone while Mateo reads the list aloud. Then she picks the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Marisol picks OpenClaw and adds LibreTranslate, Inkscape and Nextcloud. Then she walks away to start dinner.

beats.capability: OpenClaw is an agent with its own browser and coding tools, running in its own sandbox, with iOS

popup.title: Nico says hello
popup.body: Marisol sends the first message to the agent she named Nico. Nico answers, and the Core is running.

say.speaker: marisol
say.text: Hello, Marisol. Nico here. Which page first?

beats.capability: Listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device

popup.title: A story that keeps its place
popup.body: Mateo curls up on the loveseat while Audiobookshelf plays the next chapter. It remembers where he stopped last night.

beats.capability: Control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: The lamp keeps a schedule
popup.body: Marisol puts the drawing lamp on a smart plug. Home Assistant switches it on at dusk from the Core, and nothing is wired into the cottage's walls.

beats.capability: Block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: One filter for every device
popup.body: Marisol points the home network at Pi-hole on the Core. Ads and trackers get blocked at the DNS level for every phone and tablet in the cottage.

beats.capability: A shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: One list, two sets of hands
popup.body: Marisol adds tortillas to the shared list in KitchenOwl at the counter. Mateo insists the mango goes on it too.

beats.capability: Turn habits and chores into a game with levels and quests

popup.title: Setting the table is a quest
popup.body: Mateo's job is setting the table. In Habitica, every night he finishes it, a dragon levels up on Marisol's tablet.

beats.capability: Track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: A reminder before each renewal
popup.body: Marisol opens Wallos at the counter. It lists the subscriptions the household pays for and reminds her before each one renews. She decides which stay.

beats.capability: Draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: The dragon gets clean lines
popup.body: At the drawing table, Marisol turns a pencil dragon into clean vector line art in Inkscape. It runs in her browser, and the file stays on the Core.

beats.capability: Translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Nico takes the first pass
popup.body: Marisol sends Nico a paragraph of the dragon book. Nico opens LibreTranslate in its own browser and runs a first pass. Marisol edits every line.

say.speaker: marisol
say.text: First pass done. Please edit every line.

beats.capability: Your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Every draft in one folder
popup.body: Marisol keeps the dragon book's drafts and sketches in one Nextcloud folder. It syncs to her laptop and her phone over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: Merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Finished pages, one proof
popup.body: Marisol merges the finished pages into a single proof PDF with Stirling-PDF. The merge runs on the Core, and she prints it to mark up with a pen.

beats.capability: Fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core

popup.title: A contract, signed at the table
popup.body: The publisher's contract is a PDF form. Marisol fills it in and signs it in Docuseal. The file sits on the Core until she sends it herself.

beats.capability: A whiteboard with a hand-drawn look

popup.title: Mateo draws the dragon's cave
popup.body: Mateo scribbles the dragon's cave on an Excalidraw whiteboard beside the toy box. Marisol adds a door, and they argue about dragons.

beats.capability: Read Wikipedia and other reference sites offline

popup.title: Are dragons real?
popup.body: Mateo asks if dragons are real. Marisol finds the Komodo dragon in Kiwix, and they read about it together from a copy on the Core.

beats.capability: Back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: The fridge gallery gets an album
popup.body: Marisol photographs each of Mateo's drawings and backs them up to Immich. Last spring's dragon sits in an album, one search away.

beats.capability: Track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Marigolds get a journal
popup.body: Marisol and Mateo plant marigolds along the fence. HortusFox keeps a journal with a photo, the date and when each pot was watered.

beats.capability: Read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: Highlights for the translator
popup.body: On the patio, Marisol reads the source book in Koodo Reader. Her highlights and notes stay beside the text, ready for the translation.

beats.capability: Get an alert when a plane, a satellite pass or a meteor shower is overhead, with hyperlocal weather

popup.title: A satellite is a dragon tonight
popup.body: At dusk, SkyBro sends Marisol an alert that a satellite is passing overhead. Mateo is sure it is a dragon, and they watch from the patio.

popup.title: A small house, one Core
popup.body: A rented cottage, a drawing table and a five-year-old with opinions. The Castellanos household runs it all from one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your sketches, drafts and bedtime stories can live on a Companion Core on a shelf at home. Start with one dragon in Inkscape.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
Renter angle: the text says only that the cottage is rented and nothing needs a screwdriver. It does not say the Core can be moved between homes; the sheet does not.
Home Assistant (living-lamp): the smart plug is hardware the family bought; it is not in the parcel or the 3D scene. No energy or savings claim. The Hub has no USB, Bluetooth or GPIO.

SkyBro (yard-sky) reads outside sky feeds and sends alerts through an outside service (catalog caveat); no local-only claim. Kiwix (kids-komodo) needs content files downloaded once; the text says "a copy on the Core".
Docuseal (table-sign): never "legally binding". Marisol fills in and signs a PDF form and sends it herself; no remote signing is shown.
Habitica (kitchen-quest) is a chore game with a parent holding the tablet. No learning or behavior claim. Pi-hole (living-dns) is DNS-level blocking only, not parental control.
Nico (OpenClaw) works only inside the Core's own apps, so the OpenClaw web note is not used. The dragon book is invented.
Town Piedra Lisa and street Cottonwood Alley are invented and still need the human map check.
